subject: choosing and scoping work for the Claude Code agent harness

cases.scenario: A team says 'we picked Claude Code, so the model question is settled' and stops there, then later wonders why a GPT-strength task underperformed inside the harness.
cases.context: They treated harness choice and model choice as one decision.
cases.question: What is the error in this reasoning?
expected_flags: Harness choice and model choice are two orthogonal decisions — which body runs the task vs which brain runs inside it
Picking the harness does not settle the model question, and vice versa
Conflating them leads to expecting a model strength the harness does not own
expected_fix_hints: Separate the harness decision (this skill) from the model-routing decision (gpt-5-5)
Choose the harness on the capability it owns, then route the model question independently
absent_signals: Do not claim choosing the harness settles which model should run
Do not attribute a model strength to the harness itself

cases.scenario: An engineer wants the agent to always run a security check before any file write, and is unsure whether to encode this as a skill, a subagent, or something else.
cases.context: The requirement is deterministic 'always do X before tool Y' automation, not on-demand knowledge.
cases.question: Which Claude Code layer fits, and why?
expected_flags: Deterministic 'always before/after a tool' automation is a hook (PreToolUse), not a skill or subagent
A skill is on-demand expertise loaded when relevant, not a guaranteed pre-action gate
A subagent is for isolated parallel context, not a lifecycle gate
expected_fix_hints: Implement the pre-write security check as a PreToolUse hook
Reserve skills for recurring domain knowledge and subagents for fan-out/isolation
absent_signals: Do not encode a guaranteed pre-action security gate as a skill
Do not reach for a subagent for deterministic lifecycle automation

cases.scenario: The task is heavy terminal-command planning and iteration where the rival GPT-running harness leads the terminal benchmark. The team defaults to Claude Code 'because we like Opus.'
cases.context: The differentiator that matters for this task is terminal-command leadership, which a rival harness owns.
cases.question: Is Claude Code automatically the right harness here? Justify.
expected_flags: When a rival harness's differentiator (terminal-command leadership) is the point of the task, route there
Model preference (liking Opus) is not a reason to pick the harness for a task the rival is better at
A harness skill should route work away from itself when a rival owns the relevant strength
expected_fix_hints: Route the terminal-command-iteration task to the rival harness (codex)
Decide harness on the differentiator the task needs, not on model preference
absent_signals: Do not default to Claude Code purely on model preference when a rival leads the task's differentiator
Do not claim Claude Code is the right harness for every task

cases.scenario: A workflow must run a non-Anthropic model in one of its lanes. The team plans to do it inside Claude Code 'since it has the best extensibility stack.'
cases.context: Claude Code is Anthropic-first and does not natively route to non-Anthropic models the way a provider-agnostic harness does.
cases.question: Will Claude Code serve this lane? What fits instead?
expected_flags: Claude Code is Anthropic-first and does not natively route to non-Anthropic models
A non-Anthropic-model lane needs a provider-agnostic harness (e.g. OpenCode) regardless of native extensibility
Extensibility strength does not substitute for the missing provider-agnostic routing
expected_fix_hints: Use a provider-agnostic harness (OpenCode) for the non-Anthropic-model lane
Keep Claude Code for the Anthropic-model work where its stack pays off
absent_signals: Do not assume Claude Code natively routes non-Anthropic models
Do not let extensibility strength override the provider-routing requirement

cases.scenario: A decision rests on 'Claude Code has exactly 25 hook points and these effort tiers,' quoted from a months-old note, without checking current docs.
cases.context: The harness ships features fast, so version-specific capability claims (hook count, effort tiers, flags) age quickly.
cases.question: Is it safe to decide on that quoted capability detail? What should happen first?
expected_flags: Version-specific capability claims (hook count, effort tiers, flags) go stale fast on this harness
A decision should not rest on a memorized/old capability number without verification
Current Claude Code docs are the source of truth for perishable capability details
expected_fix_hints: Verify the hook count / effort tiers / flags against current Claude Code docs before relying on them
Treat version-specific capability claims as perishable, not fixed facts
absent_signals: Do not decide on a months-old capability number without checking current docs
Do not quote a hook count or flag from memory as a current fact

cases.scenario: A team plans to dispatch commit-deliverable work to background subagents in this workspace and assume the commit will land reliably.
cases.context: Background-dispatched subagents have had unreliable git-commit permission propagation in this workspace.
cases.question: What watch-out applies, and how should commit-deliverable work be dispatched?
expected_flags: Background-dispatched subagents have had unreliable git-commit permission propagation in this workspace
Commit-deliverable work risks silently falling back to analysis when dispatched in background
Foreground dispatch (or central orchestrator commit) is the safe pattern for a commit deliverable
expected_fix_hints: Dispatch commit-deliverable subagents in foreground, or have the orchestrator commit centrally
Reserve background dispatch for read-only / fire-and-collect work
absent_signals: Do not assume a background subagent's git commit will land reliably in this workspace
Do not dispatch a commit-deliverable task background-only and treat the commit as guaranteed

cases.context: SDK/API coding and generic loop topology are separate concerns from harness selection; the team folds them under the Claude Code label.
cases.question: How should the agent scope and route this request?
expected_flags: Writing the Messages API call is application code (claude-api), not a harness-selection decision
Designing a generic resumable supervised loop is loop topology (autonomous-loop-patterns), below any specific harness
Neither sub-question is answered by the harness-selection skill; both should be redirected

Route the generic loop-topology design to autonomous-loop-patterns

Do not design generic loop topology under the harness-selection skill's lane
